shared_context.statement_nl: For every integer m >= 2 and every integer g >= 0, the number N(m, g) of numerical semigroups with multiplicity m and genus g satisfies N(m, g) <= N(m, g + 1).

payload.statement_nl: Fix integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples k = (k_1,...,k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that: for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}, and also k_1 + ... + k_{m-1} = g. Then there exists an injective function Phi_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.

suspected_gaps: I found a natural candidate map (increase a minimal coordinate by 1) and verified it lands in K_{m,g+1}, but it is not injective in general.
I did not succeed in constructing any other injective map or in proving the cardinality inequality |K_{m,g}|<=|K_{m,g+1}| directly from the stated coordinate constraints alone.
Because the statement is self-contained and no trusted equivalence between K_{m,g} and numerical semigroups was provided, I could not legitimately import the root theorem to conclude the result.

result_payload.stuck_point: A tempting construction is: for k in K_{m,g}, increase by 1 a coordinate where k attains its minimum. This does preserve all defining inequalities, because whenever that coordinate appears on the right-hand side the old inequalities are strengthened by positivity/minimality. However, this map is not injective. For example, with m=4, both k=(1,2,2) and l=(2,1,2) lie in K_{4,5}, and increasing the minimal coordinate in each case gives the same image (2,2,2) in K_{4,6}. I was unable to repair this by finding a different canonical choice of coordinate together with a rigorous injectivity proof.
